# RM2PT-authoritative 114, second project freeze

The original RM2PT files and the previous frozen 114-row input remain unchanged.
This 114-row snapshot was generated from the same laboratory parent input with the
current prompt configuration. The schema version in `manifest.json` identifies the
preparation tool, while this directory name identifies the frozen dataset revision.

On 2026-11-02, the project owner approved these three requirement clarifications for
the next freeze (not as claims about an unchanged original RM2PT contract):

| Operation | Clarification | Evidence and status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CoCoME_orderProducts_orderItem` | Require a current OrderProduct before linking a new OrderEntry. | RM2PT effect references CurrentOrderProduct at `cocome.remodel:707`; explicit project-owner approval. Original precondition at line 687 lacks this guard. |
| `CoCoME_processSale_enterItem` | State that the new SalesLineItem is stored and becomes CurrentSaleLine. | RM2PT postcondition at `cocome.remodel:450` and line 457; explicit project-owner approval. |
| `CoCoME_processSale_makeCashPayment` | Require a current Store before updating its Sales collection. | RM2PT effect at `cocome.remodel:533-534`; explicit project-owner approval. Original precondition at lines 506-510 lacks this guard. |

Only those three `description` fields changed relative to
`data/benchmark/rm2pt_authoritative_114/operations.jsonl`. Their dependent
requirement/input/task hashes changed as expected. The prompt hash changed for all
rows because this snapshot uses the current prompt configuration; no experiment
results are transferred between the two snapshots.

The Oracle files in the first freeze are candidate evaluation artifacts. Neither
this note nor historical Jest replay certifies full source fidelity, independent
expert agreement, or readiness for formal experiments.

authority.note: The source effect spells subAmount, while the source entity declares SubAmount. The project keeps the declared field spelling, not a new business rule; the original precondition has no current-order guard.
Clause-shape alignment is not a semantic fidelity or Oracle certification.

record.source_problem: The same post-state Amount is constrained independently for each OrderEntry against the operation-entry Amount. Entries with different subtotals create incompatible equalities; equal subtotals do not accumulate.
approved_postconditions: The order status becomes REQUESTED.
The final amount equals the operation-entry amount plus the sum of the subtotal of every associated OrderEntry.
Distinct OrderEntry objects with equal subtotals contribute separately.
When there are no entries, the amount remains equal to its operation-entry value.
The operation returns true.
record.correction_scope: Replace conflicting per-entry final-amount equalities with one duplicate-preserving aggregate over the associated entries. Preserve the current-order guard, REQUESTED status and Boolean success result.

authority.note: User-approved source correction: add every entry subtotal to the operation-entry amount, including equal subtotals on distinct entries; empty orders preserve the initial amount. Executable representation and full Oracle alignment remain separate checks.
Clause-shape alignment is not a semantic fidelity or Oracle certification.

record.source_problem: The projection of SalesLineItem.Subamount is declared Set(Real), leaving a collection-kind inconsistency with duplicate-preserving charging per sales line.
approved_preconditions: The current Sale exists, is incomplete, and is not yet ready for payment.
approved_postconditions: The Sale amount becomes the sum of the subtotal of every associated sales line.
Distinct sales lines with equal subtotals each contribute; subtotals are not deduplicated by numeric value.
When there are no sales lines, the Sale amount becomes zero.
The Sale becomes ready for payment.
The operation returns the resulting Sale amount.
record.correction_scope: Specify duplicate-preserving aggregation by SalesLineItem identity. Replace, rather than increment, the Sale amount with this total. Preserve the preconditions, payment-ready update and numeric return type.

authority.note: User-approved collection semantics: every sales line contributes its subtotal, including equal amounts on distinct lines. Replace Sale.Amount with the total, use zero for an empty sale, mark payment-ready and return the numeric total. Executable representation and Oracle alignment remain separate checks.

record.source_problem: Multiple OrderEntry objects can refer to the same Item. Per-entry equalities then constrain its one post-state stock against the same operation-entry stock, rather than summing the quantities.
approved_postconditions: The order status becomes RECEIVED.
For each Item referred to by this order's entries, its final stock equals its operation-entry stock plus the quantities of all this order's entries referring to that same Item.
Distinct entries referring to the same Item contribute separately, including equal quantities.
Different Items have their quantities accumulated separately.
The operation returns true.
record.fixture_identity_note: fixture_key/item_key in the examples name object identities in the test data; they do not add a model attribute or business precondition.
record.correction_scope: Replace alias-conflicting per-entry equalities with per-Item accumulation from the operation-entry stock. Preserve the existing-order guard, RECEIVED status and Boolean success result. Do not impose entry uniqueness, cascade effects or unrelated frame conditions.

authority.note: User-approved alias-aware stock semantics: for each Item, add the quantities of all this order's entries referring to that object to its operation-entry stock. Distinct entries count separately; different Items are accumulated independently. Executable representation and Oracle alignment remain separate checks.

record.source_problem: BorrowStatus is read in the restoration guard and assigned in its consequent without explicit state qualification. The processing set, restored status and countdown boundary need a consistent pre/post-state interpretation.
approved_preconditions: No additional business condition is required.
approved_postconditions: Select the users whose suspension days are positive at operation entry and reduce each selected user's days by one.
Restore NORMAL when a selected user was SUSPEND at operation entry, has zero overdue fee, and reaches zero days after the decrement.
A user who was SUSPEND and has an outstanding overdue fee remains SUSPEND even when the days reach zero.
Users whose suspension days were already zero are not processed and remain unchanged.
record.correction_scope: Qualify processing membership and prior suspension status at operation entry; evaluate the zero-day boundary after the decrement. Do not add suspension of previously NORMAL users, fee updates, new preconditions or a return value.

authority.note: User-approved state timing: select users with positive days at operation entry, decrement once, and restore previously SUSPEND users only at the post-decrement zero-day boundary with no overdue fee. Retain suspension with outstanding fees; leave initially zero-day users unchanged. Executable representation and Oracle alignment remain separate checks.

authority.note: User-approved Set result: return distinct BookCopy object identities from the selected user's unreturned Loans with fee > 0. Multiple qualifying Loans may share one returned copy; equal attribute values do not merge different objects. Existing filters and return type are preserved.
